title: Prompt techniques
task_statement: Pick the simplest prompt technique that clears a measured accuracy bar. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Few-shot examples in multishot prompts
components.first_principle: Examples show the output pattern, so Claude copies the format, tone, and structure they show.

nodes.label: Eval results decide the example set

steps: Write 3 to 5 examples that mirror the real input and output.
Include edge cases, and vary the examples so Claude does not copy one pattern.
Wrap each example in example tags, and group the examples in examples tags.
Keep the instructions and the task in their own tags.
Place long documents above the query, instructions, and examples.
Measure accuracy with and without the examples in your evals.
Remove each example that does not change the eval result.
pros: Examples improve accuracy and consistency when they mirror the use case.
Examples change the prompt only, not the model.
Worked examples shape how Claude approaches similar problems with thinking on.
cons: Each example adds input tokens to every request.
Examples that do not match the real input can teach the wrong pattern.
A narrow example set can make the output rigid (Inference).
use_when: The output needs a fixed format, tone, or structure.
The task has edge cases that instructions describe poorly.
do_not_use_when: The zero-shot eval already passes the bar.
The examples would expose private data that the prompt must not reveal.

constraints.choice: Use 3 to 5 examples, which the docs call best results.
constraints.combination: Cache the example block when many requests share it.

constraints.choice: Keep the example set short to reduce input tokens per call.
constraints.combination: Cache the stable example block, so later calls read it from the cache.

constraints.choice: Run the evals again after each example change.
Store each example set with the template version it supports.

components.exam_tie: D2.3. Expect a scenario that asks which technique to try first against a measured accuracy bar. (Inference)
components.trap: More examples look like more guidance, but a set that lacks variety teaches an unintended pattern.
components.decision_rule: Add 3 to 5 diverse examples in example tags, then measure the result before you add more.
components.exam_tip: When examples fail, check that they mirror the real input before you add more examples.

key_facts.text: Include 3 to 5 examples for best results.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Wrap examples in example tags, and wrap multiple examples in examples tags.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Examples steer output format, tone, and structure.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Multishot examples work with thinking when each example shows a problem, a method, and an answer.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Examples should mirror the actual use case and vary enough to avoid unintended patterns.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Queries at the end of a long prompt can improve response quality by up to 30 percent in tests.
key_facts.label: Fact

components.name: Adaptive thinking and manual chain of thought
components.first_principle: Adaptive thinking gives the model room to reason, so manual step prompts are a fallback when thinking is off.
steps: Omit the thinking field on Claude Haiku 5.5 to use adaptive thinking.
Set the effort level to steer how much the model thinks.
Prefer general instructions over hand-written step plans.
When thinking is off, ask for reasoning before the answer.
Put the final answer in answer tags so code can extract it.
Leave room in max_tokens for thinking blocks.
pros: Adaptive thinking decides the depth for each request.
Answer tags let code extract the final answer.
On Claude Haiku 5.5, thinking blocks stay preserved by default.
cons: Thinking can be turned off on Claude Haiku 5.5 only at high effort or below.
Thinking tokens count toward the context window.
On Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Sonnet 5.5, a prompt that asks for written reasoning in thinking tags may be declined.
use_when: A hard task needs reasoning before a short answer.
Code extracts the answer from tags after the model reasons.
do_not_use_when: A simple lookup passes the eval bar without reasoning.
The request forces tool use with manual extended thinking, which returns an error.

constraints.choice: Use lower effort when the reasoning step is not needed.
constraints.combination: For forced tool use, check the model first, because Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, and Claude Fable 5.1 reject it.
Raise effort only for the subset that misses the floor.

constraints.choice: Use adaptive thinking across multistep tool workflows.
constraints.combination: Preserve thinking blocks when you send tool results back.

constraints.choice: Log the thinking and output token counts from the usage fields.

components.exam_tie: D2.3. Expect a scenario that asks whether explicit reasoning helps before a larger technique. (Inference)
components.trap: A step-by-step plan in every prompt looks thorough, but adaptive thinking often reasons better without one.
components.decision_rule: Use adaptive thinking first. Use a manual step prompt only when thinking is off.
components.exam_tip: On Claude Haiku 5.5, a budget_tokens setting returns a 400 error, so use the effort level instead.

key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Forced tool use works with adaptive thinking. Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Mythos 5.1 reject it with a 400 error.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Thinking tokens count toward the context window limit.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The default effort for Claude Haiku 5.5 is medium.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.label: Fact

components.name: Prefill replacement
components.first_principle: Claude 4.6 and later reject a prefilled final turn, so each prefill goal moves into the prompt or a schema.

nodes.label: Prefill on the final assistant turn
Instructions in system or user turn
Structured outputs or a tool schema

steps: Find each prefill in your requests, and write down the goal it serves.
Remove the prefill from the final assistant turn on Claude 4.6 and later.
Ask for the format in the system prompt, such as a direct answer without preamble.
Use structured outputs to constrain the response shape.
Use a tool with an enum field, or structured outputs, for classification.
Move any continuation text into the user message with the interrupted response.
pros: Structured outputs and tools enforce the shape without a prefill.
Instructions in the user message avoid the 400 error.
Earlier models still accept a prefill on the final assistant turn.
cons: A preamble can still appear, so strip it in code if it slips through.
A continuation needs the interrupted text in the user message.
The migration changes prompts, parsers, and retry logic in your code (Inference).
On Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5, forced tool use returns a 400 error, so a classification tool needs tool_choice auto.
use_when: The call targets Claude 4.6 or a later model.
The prefill only forced a format or removed a preamble.
do_not_use_when: The target model is earlier than Claude 4.6 and the prefill passes your evals.
The migration would change behavior that your evals already approve.

constraints.choice: Run the evals again after you remove each prefill.
Structured outputs add format instructions and input tokens.
constraints.combination: Use tags in the prompt when the required shape is simple.

constraints.choice: Record which prefills you removed and why.
Apply the same migration to every endpoint that sends a prefill.

components.exam_tie: D2.3. Expect a scenario where a prefill returns a 400 error on a newer model. (Inference)
components.trap: A repeat of the same prefill, unchanged, looks like a small fix, but the 400 error repeats on Claude 4.6 and later.
components.decision_rule: On Claude 4.6 and later, replace each prefill with instructions, structured outputs, or a tool.
components.exam_tip: A 400 error on a final assistant turn points to a prefill, so remove it before you change other settings.

key_facts.text: Claude 4.6 and later models reject a prefilled final assistant turn with a 400 error.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Earlier models continue to support prefills on the final assistant turn.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: On earlier models, you cannot prefill the assistant response while thinking is on.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Assistant messages added elsewhere in the conversation are not affected.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Structured outputs constrain Claude responses to a schema.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Mythos 5.1 reject forced tool use. Use tool_choice auto with strict tool use or structured outputs.
key_facts.label: Fact
